faq.q: Why are they called Abrahamic religions?
faq.a: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are called Abrahamic because all three trace their faith in one God back to Abraham, called Ibrahim in Arabic, whom they honour as a father of faith.

In the Hebrew Bible, the Christian Bible and the Quran, Abraham is the man who trusted in one God, left his home at God's call, and was promised many descendants. He is honoured as a patriarch in Judaism, a father of faith in Christianity, and a prophet in Islam.

faq.q: Do Jews, Christians and Muslims worship the same God?
faq.a: All three believe in one God, the God of Abraham, and many believers say they worship the same God. They differ in how they understand God, for example Christians believe in the Trinity, while Jews and Muslims stress that God is strictly one.
asks: Is Allah the same God as the Christian God?

faq.q: Which prophets do Judaism, Christianity and Islam share?
faq.a: They share many figures, including Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, David and Solomon. Christians and Muslims both honour Jesus and Mary, in different ways. Muslims also honour the Prophet Muhammad as the final prophet.

faq.q: How do the three faiths see Jesus?
faq.a: For Christians, Jesus is the Messiah and the Son of God who rose from the dead. In Islam, Isa is one of the greatest prophets, born of Mary, but not divine. Judaism sees him as a Jewish teacher, not the Messiah.
asks: What do Jews think of Jesus?

faq.q: Why is Jerusalem holy to three religions?
faq.a: For Jews, it is the site of the ancient Temple, and the Western Wall is a place of prayer. For Christians, it is where Jesus died and, they believe, rose again. For Muslims, Al-Aqsa Mosque is the third holiest site, linked with the Prophet Muhammad's Night Journey.
asks: Why do Jews, Christians and Muslims care about Jerusalem?

faq.a: They were Abraham's two sons, Ishmael born to Hagar and Isaac born to Sarah. Jewish tradition traces the people of Israel through Isaac and his son Jacob, while Islamic tradition honours Ishmael, called Ismail, who helped Ibrahim build the Kaaba.

faq.q: What are the holy books of the Abrahamic religions?
faq.a: Judaism has the Tanakh, whose first part is the Torah. Christianity has the Bible, with the Old Testament, which overlaps with the Tanakh, and the New Testament. Islam has the Quran.

faq.q: What does People of the Book mean?
faq.a: People of the Book is a phrase in the Quran for Jews and Christians, who, like Muslims, received scriptures from God. It recognises a shared heritage of revelation.
asks: Who are the People of the Book?

faq.q: What do the Abrahamic religions have in common?
faq.a: They share belief in one God who created the world, prophets who brought God's message, holy scriptures, prayer, charity, a moral law, and belief in a judgement and life after death.
asks: Similarities between Judaism, Christianity and Islam?
What do the three religions share?

faq.q: What are the main differences between them?
faq.a: They differ over who were God's final messengers and scriptures, and especially over Jesus: Messiah and Son of God for Christians, prophet for Muslims, and not the Messiah for Jews. They also differ in practices, festivals and laws.
asks: Differences between Judaism, Christianity and Islam?
How are the Abrahamic religions different?

faq.q: Which Abrahamic religion is the oldest?
faq.a: Judaism is the oldest, with roots more than 3,000 years ago. Christianity began about 2,000 years ago among Jesus' Jewish followers, and Islam began in the 600s CE with the Prophet Muhammad.
asks: Which came first, Judaism, Christianity or Islam?

faq.a: Yes. Smaller faiths are sometimes included too, such as the Baha'i Faith, the Druze, and the Samaritans, because they also honour Abraham and believe in one God.

facts: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are called the Abrahamic religions because they honour Abraham, called Ibrahim in Arabic.
